current.title: Pharmacological and Device-Based Intervention for Preventing Heart Failure After Acute Myocardial Infarction - A Clinical Review
current.citation: Saito Y, Kobayashi Y, Tsujita K, et al. Pharmacological and Device-Based Intervention for Preventing Heart Failure After Acute Myocardial Infarction - A Clinical Review. Circ J. 2024;88(11):1727-1736. PMID 39284720. doi:10.1253/circj.CJ-24-0633.
current.publicationGuard: Require documented acute myocardial infarction and separately documented new or materially worsened heart failure developing in the clinically relevant post-infarction period, with appropriate evidence of ventricular dysfunction and/or a clinically established heart-failure syndrome. Do not infer heart failure from myocardial infarction alone, and do not attribute pre-existing heart failure to a later infarction without evidence of material post-infarction worsening.

current.title: Pulmonary Vascular Disease in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
current.citation: Kay D, Bernardo R, Elwing J. Pulmonary Vascular Disease in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease. Semin Respir Crit Care Med. 2024;45(5):574-581. PMID 39532092. doi:10.1055/s-0044-1791824.
current.publicationGuard: Require documented COPD and separately established pulmonary hypertension clinically attributable to chronic lung disease/COPD, preferably with appropriate hemodynamic confirmation when clinically available. Evaluate alternative causes of pulmonary hypertension, including left-heart disease, chronic thromboembolic disease, and other pulmonary vascular disorders. Do not infer pulmonary hypertension from COPD severity, hypoxemia, dyspnea, or an elevated echocardiographic estimate alone.

current.title: Factors Associated With Persisting Symptoms After Concussion in Adults With Mild TBI: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
current.citation: McIntosh SJ, Vergeer MH, Galarneau JM, Eliason PH, Debert CT. Factors Associated With Persisting Symptoms After Concussion in Adults With Mild TBI: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. JAMA Netw Open. 2025;8(6):e2516619. PMID 40531530. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2025.16619.
current.publicationGuard: Require documented mild traumatic brain injury/concussion followed by separately documented persistent post-concussive symptoms extending beyond the acute recovery period, with clinical attribution to the qualifying injury. Do not infer post-concussion syndrome from transient acute headache, dizziness, cognitive complaints, or other symptoms occurring only immediately after injury. Consider pre-existing psychiatric, sleep, neurologic, and symptom conditions that may contribute to or mimic persistent post-concussive symptoms.

current.title: Reassessing Bladder Recovery in Cauda Equina Syndrome: Long-Term Outcomes After Surgical Decompression - A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
current.citation: Najjar E, Muscogliati R, Trumble C, et al. Reassessing Bladder Recovery in Cauda Equina Syndrome: Long-Term Outcomes After Surgical Decompression - A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Spine J. 2026 Jul 21;S1529-9430(26)00582-6. Online ahead of print. PMID 42480656. doi:10.1016/j.spinee.2026.07.005.
current.publicationGuard: Require documented cauda equina syndrome and separately documented urinary incontinence or persistent loss of urinary continence attributable to the CES neurologic injury. Do not map urinary retention alone, nonspecific lower urinary tract symptoms, catheter use, or unrelated urologic disease to urinary-incontinence. Establish the bladder phenotype and temporal relationship to CES, and consider competing urologic or neurologic causes where clinically relevant.

finalApproved.title: Reassessing Bladder Recovery in Cauda Equina Syndrome: Long-Term Outcomes After Surgical Decompression - A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
finalApproved.citation: Najjar E, Muscogliati R, Trumble C, et al. Reassessing Bladder Recovery in Cauda Equina Syndrome: Long-Term Outcomes After Surgical Decompression - A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Spine J. 2026 Jul 21;S1529-9430(26)00582-6. Online ahead of print. PMID 42480656. doi:10.1016/j.spinee.2026.07.005.
finalApproved.publicationGuard: Require documented cauda equina syndrome secondary to degenerative lumbar spine disease, with separately documented urinary incontinence or persistent loss of urinary continence attributable to the CES neurologic injury. Where the proposition concerns a persistent postoperative residual, require an appropriate post-decompression temporal course. Do not map urinary retention alone, nonspecific lower urinary tract symptoms, catheter use, or unrelated urologic disease to urinary-incontinence. Establish the bladder phenotype and temporal relationship to CES, and consider competing urologic or neurologic causes where clinically relevant.
